texts.preamble: Mrs.Jasmine vs Mr.Georgekutty John on 11 March, 2020 In The Court Of Metropolitan Magistrate Traffic Court - V, Bengaluru Present : Smt.Pooja Shetti B.A., Ll.B. (Hon's). M.M.T.C - V, Bengaluru Dated This 11th Day Of March 2020 Crl. Misc.No.240 - 2013 Petitioner : Mrs.Jasmine, Aged about 42 years, W/o.Mr.Georgekutty John, D/o.Mr.Jose Mathew, R/at.No.31, Katha No.295/2, Chamundeswari Layout, Devarachikkanahalli Road, Near St.Mary's Crescent School, Begur, Bengaluru - 560 068. // Vs // Respondent : Mr.Georgekutty John, Aged about 45 years, S/o.Mr.Ulahannan Pulickal @ John, R/at.Pulickal House, Paingottoor Kara, Pothanicadu Village, Kothamangalam Taluk. Also Working at: Fire Station, Alure, Alwaye, Ernakumal District, Kerala.
texts.facts: This is the petition filed by the petitioner against the respondent under section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence At., 2005 (herein after referred as P.W.D.V. Act, 2005) seeking various relief. 2. The brief facts of the petitioners case is as follows; The marriage between the petitioner and respondent was solemnized on 15.11.1998 at St.Anthony's Forane Church, Kerala as per Christian Customs. Out of their wedlock, they have two children. It is Mrs.Jasmine vs Mr.Georgekutty John on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38013752/ 1 the submission of the petitioner that, at the time of marriage, respondent was working as Head Constable in BSF. However, he has informed petitioner and her parents that, he is working as Nursing Superintendent at BSF and he would obtain immediate transfer to Bengaluru to join the petitioner. At the time of marriage, the petitioner was working and living at Bengaluru. After marriage, the petitioner and respondent had stayed for 15 days at his parents house, thereafter the respondent had lived in different places due to his work and he used to join the petitioner during vacation. From March 2011, parties are living separately. The petitioner further submits that, before marriage itself, her parents had enquired the respondent and his parents about the expectation of dowry, whey they demanded no dowry, the petitioner and her parents agreed to the marriage. However, when the petitioner was taken for purchase of wedding dress, the respondent and his parents demanded Rs.50,000/- as dowry or asked to transfer property standing in the name of her parents to the name of respondent. Hence, the petitioner went back without purchasing the dress, however the respondent immediately went to petitioner's house and contended that, his parents are not happy with the marriage and he has no role in dowry demand, hence the petitioner believed him and proceed to marry him. After the marriage, the petitioner found that, respondent was a short tempered person. After the marriage, when the petitioner and respondent went to petitioners place for first time on the way, her friends and relatives were talking to her, hence the respondent got angry and left behind the petitioner. Thereafter, petitioner along with the respondent went to home warming ceremony of one of respondent's friend, wherein husband of one of respondent's class mate inquired the petitioner about her family, job etc., for which the respondent got furious and shouted on the petitioner and left the place with her. The respondent used to take out his anger on the petitioner and later he used to apolize for his deed, after 15 days of marriage, the respondent went back to his job. The petitioner further submits that, whenever there was vacation, the respondent used to come back, however his behavior towards the petitioner was very rude, even during her pregnancy, the respondent failed to provide basic necessities to the petitioner. After her 1st delivery, when petitioners co-brother hit slightly on the head of the petitioner, as she was feeling uneasy and coughing, as some water went to her nose, the respondent got angry and when her co-brother left, he abused the petitioner physically in the hospital. In the year 2009, twice the respondent came and he has tortured the petitioner both physically and mentally, whenever he was outside the matrimonial house, he did not helped the petitioner to meet household and child's expenses. Further, the respondent always used to suspect the character of the petitioner and she was not allowed to talk to anybody, if the petitioner talks to auto driver, bus conductor, neighbors etc., the respondent used to suspect her. The petitioner further submits that, during the delivery of 2nd child, the respondent was present at the Bengaluru but he did not paid hospital bills, which came up to Rs.30,000/-, however he gave Rs.5,000/- and immediately went to Kerala, hence it is her parents who had arranged money for hospital bills. Further, he has failed to meet the education expenses of her children, hence as there was no option, the petitioner had pledged her gold jewellaries to pay the school fees. The respondent has harassed the petitioner without giving money towards their expenses. According to petitioner, twice the respondent has called her stating that, he has lost his purse and luggage and asked her to deposit money to his account. Believing the same, the petitioner has tried to help in all possible ways. The petitioner further contends that, the respondent used to pick up quarrel with the people without any reason. Whenever they went out for dinner, the respondent used to pick up quarrel with the hotel staff staying that, price of the food is high and quality is low. Further, when the barber demanded Rs.25/- for hair cutting of the child, the Mrs.Jasmine vs Mr.Georgekutty John on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38013752/ 2 respondent argued saying at Assam it will cost only Rs.5/- and return home without getting hair cut done. The petitioner further submits that, except her residential property which stands in the joint name of the petitioner and respondent, the respondent has not brought anything to the petitioner and her children. During their 14 years of marriage, the respondent has brought only two night dress for petitioner, three dresses for their son and two dresses for their daughter. The petitioner further submits that, after obtaining voluntary retirement, the respondent quit two jobs after picking up quarrel with the co-workers and now he is working in fire force department at Kerala. The respondents various acts omission conduct and commission has caused serious domestic violence to the petitioner and her children's, he has failed to support them economically. Due to the harassment, the petitioner is suffering from immense, anxiety, stress etc., for which the respondent assumed that, petitioner is suffering from tuberculosis and forced the children not to go near her. Thereafter, the petitioner consulted doctor at St.John's Medical College and Hospital, wherein the doctor informed the respondent that, the petitioners health condition is normal. Thereafter, the petitioner informed about the behavior of the respondent to his brother and sister, however they did not interfere. The petitioner further submits that, after intervention of her family members and contribution of money from her parents, the respondent agreed to buy a house in Bengaluru., for purchase and construction of house, they have spent Rs.35,00,000/- out of which, the respondent had contributed only Rs.17,00,000/- remaining money was arranged by her parents and she has also availed hand loans and had mortgaged her jewellaries. Thereafter, as per the advise of the respondent, the petitioner had pledged her gold ornaments in his bank, however after paying 5 installments, the respondent refused to pay the remaining installments, hence the petitioner took entire gold and mortgaged it in another bank, now she is unable to pay the installment towards the said mortgage. After shifting to new house, the respondents behavior became more temper mental, angry, frustrated etc., and he used to frequently shout at the applicant and at the tenants. Further, he failed to provide maintenance to the petitioner and her children. There was a due of Rs.5,50,000/- to the contractor of the house and the respondent started to accuse the petitioner stating that, she is having relationship with the said contractor. The petitioner further submits that, the respondent used to suspect her character and refused to pay educational expenses of her children. According to petitioner, on one such occasion, respondent had thrown holy book and destroyed holy photos and threatened to kill the petitioner and had thrown the petitioner and children out of matrimonial house and after creating huge fight, he left to his native village at Kerala. Thereafter, the petitioner went to her parents house and when they came to know about the life threat, they called the respondent and tried to convince him, wherein the respondent had appolized in writing for his behavior and had given assurance that, he will take care of the petitioner and her children. After the said incident, the respondents stayed at his house in Kerala and did not came back for 6 months. Thereafter, the respondent again started to suspect the character of the petitioner and became more violent. During November, 2011 he came to Bengaluru in the pretext of attending birth day of their daughter and he picked up fight with the petitioner and her father, meanwhile he had broken a window glass, hence he got himself injured and assaulted the petitioner and her children, thereafter fearing their safety, petitioner informed the Electronic City Police and lodged complaint ton 21.11.2011, wherein police called the respondent and advised him. Petitioner also informed about the same to his siblings, they also advised him, then the respondent left the matrimonial house and stayed in his parents house for several months. The petitioner further submits that, in spite of all these abuses, she did not filed petition seeking divorce with the hope Mrs.Jasmine vs Mr.Georgekutty John on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38013752/ 3 that, the respondent may change, however whenever the respondent visits, petitioner and her children, he subjects them to domestic violence. According to petitioner, respondent is interested in unnatural and oral sex and he compels the petitioner to fulfill his demand, he also makes allegation against the character of the petitioner stating that, she has relationship with tenants, taxi driver, vegetable seller etc., including her father who is aged about 70 years. According to petitioner, in spite of several panchayaths including panchayath held by priest of the church, the respondent did not changed his behavior, and he is staying separately from March - 2011, however he was visiting petitioner during weekends and holidays and during those visits, he subjects them to domestic violence . On 09.08.2013, the respondent came to Bengaluru and started to abuse the petitioner stating that, she has illegal relationship with her old tenant who had come to collect his belongings kept in the house of the petitioner. He forcibly pushed the petitioner, her father and daughter out of the house, hence after taking shelter at tenants house, they left to their native. Thereafter, petitioner lodged complaint against the respondent at Kalloorkadu Circle office, Kerala, wherein the respondent appolized and assured not to commit such act in future. According to petitioner, from last 3 years, she is trying to escape from domestic violence and she is taking care of children, single handedly, now she is unable to work and she has no job. Hence, the children's are dependant on the rent received from their upstairs portion of the house, which is let out for two families. In spite of having pension of more than of Rs.25,000/- per month and salary of Rs.20,000/- per month, the respondent is not providing any monetary help towards the educational expenses of the children, he also discourages children from study, he calls the petitioner repeatedly and uses abusive words. Further, he is paying nothing towards the loan incurred for the construction of house, apart from that, he is also posing threat to the life and limb of the petitioner. According to petitioner, during October - 2013 Dasara Holidays, when she, her father and children went to Chattisgad to attend a function, the respondent without fear of law destroyed all the articles at the home damaged washing machine and intimated the petitioner over mobile phone and threatened her with dire consequences, hence, the petitioner lodged complaint at Electronic City Police Station. Hence, there is continuous act of domestic violence. Hence, the petition. 3. After the registration of the petition, the notice was sent to the respondent through RPAD and P.O. Respondent appeared through his advocate and filed his objections to the main petition. On the other hand, respondent in his objections to main petition denied all the allegations made by the petitioner. However, the respondent admits his marriage with the petitioner and contends that, petitioner has filed false complaint only to harass him. According to respondent, he took voluntary retirement from service in the year 2009. On 06.09.2013, petitioner left the respondent and from then parties are living separately, there was no demand for dowry or property by the respondent and his parents. During her stay in the parental house of the respondent, petitioner showed negative attitude towards the respondent and his parents and called his family members as uncultured and according to her, they have no manners as to how to behave. According to respondent, petitioner wanted to separate him from his family and wanted to stay at Bengaluru, hence they shifted to Bengaluru. According to respondent, when he was in service, during vacation he used to come to Bengaluru and live with the petitioner. During those days, he used to bring dress, costumes and other articles to the petitioner, however she was not happy and she used to compare the respondent with others and used to quarrel with him for silly reasons. According to respondent, petitioner was Mrs.Jasmine vs Mr.Georgekutty John on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38013752/ 4 never willing to visit his parents house. According to respondent, he wanted to take care of his aged mother and brother, as he is the only bread winner of the family, however the petitioner did not allowed him and asked to register property in her name. During her pregnancy, he has provided medical care and attention to her. Even after delivery, it is him who has paid all the expenses and took the petitioner and the child to the house, however within one month of delivery, when the respondent saw that, petitioner is watching TV, he switched off the TV, hence she got furious and abused him. According to respondent, petitioner used to spend money on cosmetics and beauty parlors and when he try to convince her, she became angry and compared her life with the life of her friends. According to respondent, he has discharged his duties and responsibilities as a father and husband, he has paid school fee, medical expenses, etc., however petitioner is quarrelsome and did not bothered about the studies and future of the children. When the respondent questioned the same, the petitioner used to shout at him. According to respondent, he is not a drunkard, however when he arrived on leave, he noticed that, petitioner spends long time in talking over phone and spend little time with the children. The petitioner never had the patience to hear the respondent and he has committed no act of domestic violence against her. He is concerned about the future of children, hence he was forced to take voluntary retirement. As he wanted to settle down and lived together with his family, he thought of constructing new house at Bengaluru. According to respondent, a total amount of Rs.33,40,000/- was spent for the purchase of site and construction of the shared household mentioned in the petition. Rs.14,40,000/- was spent for the purchase of site in Chamundeshwari Layout, Devarachikkanahalli Road, Begur, Bengaluru and Rs.19,00,000/- for construction of the house, Rs.21,00,000/- was contributed by the respondent from pension, P.F, gratuity, other allowances and savings and through the sale of the property of Rs.12.25 cents of the respondent in Kaliyar in Kerala and Rs.12,00,000/- was got from the applicant's family as her share. The above said shared household is in the joint name of the applicant and respondent. In the above said shared household, all household articles and furniture were brought by the respondent. Thereafter, they shifted to new house, however petitioner started to ill-treat him due to the wrong advise of her sister. According to respondent, on 14.01.2011, he asked the petitioner to resign the job as it requires soliciting the customers, hence the petitioner got angry, she destroyed household articles and filed false complaint before Electronic City Police Station. Thereafter, with the intervention of father of the petitioner, the matter was amicably settled. According to respondent, the petitioner is getting Rs.14,750/- as rent from the building and Rs.15,000/- as interest from the security amount, apart from that, she also has salary. The respondent further submits that, on 09.08.2013, he saw the petitioner coming late in somebody's car, when he asked about the same, she got angry and tried to attack him with knife, when he ran out of the house she locked the door and did not allowed him to enter the house. Thereafter, on 19.08.2013 she filed complaint at Kalloorkad Police Station, alleging domestic violence. Thereafter, police conducted conciliation and the settlement was arrived. As per the agreement, on completion of academic year petitioner and her children, were supposed to return paingottoor by selling the house at Bengaluru. Thereafter, petitioner returned to Bengaluru on 06.09.2013, with the promise that, she will return after the Dasara Holidays, but thereafter, she did not return and asked the respondent not to come to Bengaluru, hence the petitioner herself without any sufficient reason. Thereafter, respondent has filed petition seeking restitution of conjugal right against the petitioner in O.P.No.79/2014, hence as the petitioner herself has left the respondent, hence she is not entitled to any of the relief claimed. Hence, prays to dismiss the petition. Mrs.Jasmine vs Mr.Georgekutty John on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38013752/ 5 ]] 4. In order to prove the contention of the 1st petitioner, she examined herself as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of her examination-in-chief and Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.40 are marked. On the other hand, despite the reasonable opportunity given to the respondent, respondent did not cross-examined PW.1 and did not adduced his side evidence, hence, respondent evidence is taken as nil. 5. Perused both the documentary and oral evidence.
texts.arguments: The petitioner further contends that, after marriage she came to know that, the respondent is short tempered and he used to suspect the character of the petitioner. On the other hand, in the objection, the respondent denied all the allegations and contended that, petitioner herself has withdrawn from the company of the respondent without sufficient reason. Hence, he has filed petition seeking restitution of conjugal right against her. However, in spite of several opportunity, the respondent failed to cross-examine PW.1. On perusal of Ex.P.39, it is the Judgment of Hon'ble Family Court at Muvattupizha in O.P.No.79/2014, wherein the respondent has filed petition seeking restitution of conjugal right, the Hon'ble Family Court while dismissing the said application, has held that, the respondent herein has made baseless allegations against the petitioner herein, hence the petitioner herein has sufficient and justifiable cause for withdrawing herself from the society of respondent herein. 12. In the present petition also the respondent makes allegation that, on 09.08.2013 he has seen petitioner coming late in someone's car. However, the respondent fails to prove his allegation against the petitioner, making baseless allegation against character of woman amounts emotional abuse. Further, in Vijaykumar Ramachandra Bhate Vs. Neela Vijaykumar Bhate, 2003(6) SCC 334, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that, character assassination of wife by Appellant husband in the written statement constitutes mental cruelty for sustaining the claim for divorce under section 13(1)(i-a) of Hindu Marriage Act. The Hon'ble Court further held that, leveling, disgusting accusations of unchastely and indecent familiarities with the person out side wedlock and allegations of extra marital relationship is a grave assault on character, honor, reputation, status as well as health of the wife. 13. With respect to economic abuse, it is the contention of the petitioner that, the respondent has failed to provide education expenses to her children and basic necessities to herself and her children. In support of her contention, she has produced documents pertaining to expenses of her children and got them marked as Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.24 and Ex.P.31 to Ex.P.36. As the respondent failed to cross-examine the petitioner, her contention stands unchallenged and it is supported by above mentioned exhibits. In order to prove that, gold ornaments has been pledged, petitioner has produced Ex.P.5 to Ex.P.8, however on perusal of the same, those documents neither contents the name of the petitioner nor respondent, hence petitioner fails to prove her allegations of pleading of gold. The petitioner further contended that, respondent used to visit the matrimonial house again and again and troubling her. In support of her contention, she has produced certified copy of complaint dated 15.05.2015 and FIR filed by Electronic City Police on 15.05.2015. The petitioner further contended that, for the purchase and construction of house, respondent has paid only Rs.17,00,000/- and remaining Rs.18,00,000/- has been arranged by her parents and herself by availing hand loans and by mortgage of jewellaries.
